question: Does one LiMT-style return/volatility model outperform two independently trained specialists?
price_definition: Existing CRSP price-return target (not a price level): dlyretx at t+2, signal t, execution t+1 close.
volatility_definition: Existing t+2 high-low range divided by OHLC4; a range proxy, not realized standard deviation.
architecture: Pinned full LiMT encoder and eight shared experts. Remove the volume branch and unused feature gate. Joint retains the released one-way volatility-hidden-to-return fusion, using its original second gate row. Specialists retain the same initialized encoder/experts and their own task gate/head only, with no cross-task fusion. Thus this measures joint supervision plus LiMT task fusion, not the isolated causal effect of parameter sharing.
initialization: For each seed, initialize the complete pinned LiMT identically before extracting active branches; all common parameters start equal. Reset training RNG identically after construction.

training.loss: Mean of per-task cross-sectional MSEs on the existing daily standardized targets; joint equal weights 0.5/0.5, each specialist weight 1. Missing labels masked before arithmetic.
training.selection: One joint checkpoint selected by equal mean of validation return IC and volatility IC; each specialist selected by its own validation IC. Same cap and patience. No test-based selection.
training.sensitivity: Additionally save each joint task's own validation-IC-best checkpoint from the same training trajectory. These need two checkpoint deployments and are explicitly secondary.
training.precision: FP32 parameters/activations, CUDA TF32 permitted, no mixed precision
training.batch: One complete 500-stock cross-section; deterministic date shuffle seed+epoch.

evaluation.population: Unchanged historical US 500-stock panel, features, normalization, lookback, splits and purged label boundaries from the base protocol.
evaluation.primary: For each target compare mean daily cross-sectional Pearson IC of the three-seed score ensembles on exactly the same observations, dates and targets. Positive joint-minus-specialist IC favors joint.
evaluation.primary_family: Two two-sided HAC20 tests, Holm adjustment across return and volatility. Claim joint outperforms both only if both differences are positive and both adjusted p-values <0.05. Otherwise identify the supported outcome or report inconclusive.
evaluation.secondary: Daily Spearman RankIC and daily normalized MSE, four tests adjusted together with Holm, descriptive calendar-year effects and per-seed comparisons. Positive specialist-minus-joint MSE favors joint. MSE is in daily target-z-score units, not raw price or volatility units.
evaluation.dependence: Unique trading dates are sampling units; intercept-only OLS, Bartlett HAC20, small-sample correction and t intervals. HAC5/HAC60 and 5000 circular bootstrap means with blocks20/60 are sensitivities. Seeds are diagnostics, not independent daily samples.
evaluation.checkpoint_sensitivity: Repeat ensemble comparisons with per-task-selected joint checkpoints; exploratory, not a second chance to pass the primary test.
evaluation.test_windows: Primary full 2017-2025; calendar-year effects descriptive only.
evaluation.limits: Retrospective follow-up on a previously analyzed panel; not a pristine new holdout or prospective evidence. Does not test price levels, realized volatility, trading profitability, other task weights or other architectures. Equal loss weights are fixed without a search.
